discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 090713
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
213 AM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Remaining dry with above normal temperatures today into Tuesday. 

- A chance for rain (40-70%) late Wednesday into Thursday.

- Cooler weather and lingering chances for lake effect showers into 
  Thursday night and Friday.  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 213 AM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

Tranquil wx conditions and warmer than average temperatures will 
persist today into Tuesday on the southern fringes of broad west-
northwest flow aloft. A substantial pattern change then ushers in a 
cooler and more unsettled pattern late Wednesday through Saturday as 
an upper jet streak dives down into the MS Valley, eventually 
carving out an unseasonably strong 500 mb height minimum into the 
Great Lakes and Northeast. A leading, compact upper wave in this 
transition still looks to send a developing frontal wave southeast 
into the OH Valley and central Appalachians late Wednesday into 
Thursday morning. Dynamic nature to the wave and pacific origins 
likely allows for an area of more substantial rain coverage, 
though guidance still diverges regarding the track of the system
currently over the north Pacific. Opted to hold with NBM mid 
chance PoPs for now given the lingering uncertainty. 

Moist and chilly cyclonic flow behind the departing low 
pressure center will keep clouds and shower chances in the 
forecast then into Thursday afternoon and Friday. This regime 
also sets up a favorable lake effect response parallel to the 
long axis of Lake MI later Thursday through as late as Saturday 
morning into far nw IN/sw MI and ne IL. Progged thermal profiles
support rain as the primary precipitation type, though it does 
seem likely that snowflakes may mix in at times inland. Ridging 
builds back Sunday into the first half of next week with a 
return to dry wx and warming temps. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 109 AM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

VFR conditions expected through this TAF period. Light
southwesterly winds will back to more southerly late tonight.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 9 AM EST this morning for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Steinwedel
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 090532

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1132 PM CST Sun Nov 08 2026

   Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms appear unlikely across the U.S. Monday through
   Monday night.

   ...South Texas...

   An upper low initially near the Big Bend region at 12z Monday is
   forecast to weaken through the day while a series of embedded
   perturbations track from the lower Rio Grande Valley along the
   coast. Forcing for ascent associated with those features along with
   persistent low/mid-level warm advection is likely to sustain
   scattered thunderstorms through the morning with areal coverage
   gradually decreasing by mid to late afternoon. 

   Similar to Sunday, the kinematic environment will feature veering
   winds with height with around 40 kt of deep-layer shear, which would
   conditionally support supercell storm modes and some severe weather
   threat. While a strong storm or two is possible Monday morning, it
   appears that outflow associated with early-day convection is likely
   to limit more robust air mass destabilization and an associated
   severe weather threat.


   ...Pacific Northwest...

   A short-wave trough is forecast to move onshore Monday afternoon
   with associated height falls/midlevel cooling coinciding with moist,
   onshore flow in the low levels. Those processes will yield weak
   instability (MUCAPE of 100-200 J/kg) with forecast soundings
   indicating the potential for convective updrafts to reach sufficient
   depth for episodic lightning activity from the coast inland to at
   least the Cascades Monday afternoon and evening. Somewhat analogous
   to Saturday, strong low-level winds are forecast ahead of the
   surface front, suggesting some potential for a few strong wind gusts
   in association with any deeper convective elements moving onshore.


   ...South Florida...

   A few lightning strikes may occur with diurnally enhanced
   thunderstorms Monday afternoon amidst a moist and marginally
   unstable air mass. However, forecast soundings indicate a warm and
   dry nose centered in the 650-600 mb layer, which will likely inhibit
   the majority of convective updrafts from reaching sufficient depth
   for lightning discharge.

   ..Mead.. 11/09/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 090636

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1236 AM CST Mon Nov 09 2026

   Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe threat is forecast across the U.S. Tuesday and Tuesday
   night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At mid-levels, west-northwesterly flow will remain in place on
   Tuesday across much of the U.S. Within the flow, a shortwave trough
   will move eastward across the southern Plains. Ahead of the trough,
   isolated thunderstorms will be possible along the Texas Gulf Coast
   from Tuesday into Tuesday night. No severe threat is expected, and
   no thunderstorms are forecast across the remainder of the
   continental U.S.

   ..Broyles.. 11/09/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 090717

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0117 AM CST Mon Nov 09 2026

   Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe threat is forecast across the U.S. Wednesday and Wednesday
   night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At upper-levels, a ridge will move eastward across the western U.S.
   on Wednesday, as a trough and an associated cold front move
   southeastward into the mid Mississippi Valley. Ahead of the front,
   thunderstorms will be possible in the afternoon from Illinois
   southward into western Tennessee. A strong wind gust are two will be
   possible along this narrow north-to-south corridor. However, no
   appreciable severe threat is expected. Elsewhere, thunderstorm
   development will be possible near the coasts of southeast Texas and
   southwest Louisiana. Scattered storms will also be possible over
   parts of the Florida Peninsula. No severe threat is expected.

   ..Broyles.. 11/09/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
